notes: Sound Lab lite (US-070, S22). Each word has a clip id; a recorded clip is assets/pairs/<id>.<m4a|ogg|mp3|aac|wav>. Without one the app falls back to TTS with a 'Preview voice' label. Words in a side line up by index with the other side (vest/west, vine/wine). Which clips to record: product/06-build/content-notes.md (Q-011).

pairs.label: v / w
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. Watch for teeth on the lip.
pairs.reveal_hint: These two are close. Hear them back to back and listen for the rounded lips.
pairs.self_check: Did your lips round, with no teeth on the lip? If it sounded like "vine", try again slowly.

a.tip: top teeth rest on your lower lip, then buzz.

b.tip: round your lips like "oo", no teeth.

pairs.label: th / t
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. "th" lets air slide out; "t" stops it for a moment.
pairs.reveal_hint: Listen for the soft hiss of air in "th". "t" is a short, clean tap.
pairs.self_check: Did your tongue tip show between your teeth for "three"? If it sounded like "tree", slow down and let the air flow.

a.tip: tongue tip lightly between your teeth, then blow.

b.tip: tongue tip taps the ridge behind your top teeth.

pairs.label: s / sh
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. "s" is thin and sharp; "sh" is wider and softer.
pairs.reveal_hint: Listen for the hush: "sh" sounds wider, like asking for quiet.
pairs.self_check: Did your lips push forward for "ship"? If it sounded thin like "sip", round your lips more.

a.tip: smile a little, tongue near your top teeth, a thin hiss.

b.tip: push your lips forward, tongue a little further back.

pairs.label: z / j
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. "z" buzzes all the way; "j" starts with a tiny stop.
pairs.reveal_hint: Listen for the buzz: "z" never stops, "j" begins with a little push.
pairs.self_check: Could you feel the buzz in "zest" without a stop at the start? If it sounded like "jest", hum the "z" first.

a.tip: like "s" but with your voice on: a steady buzz.

b.tip: tongue touches the roof of your mouth, then releases.

pairs.label: i / ee
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. The long vowel is held longer, with a wider smile.
pairs.reveal_hint: Listen for the length: "ee" is held; "i" is quick and relaxed.
pairs.self_check: Was "leave" longer than "live"? If they sounded the same, stretch the "ee" and smile.

pairs.label: ड़ / र
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. ड़ flicks forward from a curled tongue; र is a light tap.
pairs.reveal_hint: In ड़ the curled tongue flicks forward; in र it only taps. Hear them back to back.
pairs.self_check: Did your tongue curl back and flick forward in मोड़? If it sounded like मोर, try again slowly.

b.tip: जीभ दाँतों के पीछे हल्के से छुए।

pairs.label: ट / त
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. ट and ड come from a curled tongue; त and द touch the teeth.
pairs.reveal_hint: ट and ड sound heavier because the tongue curls back; त and द are lighter, at the teeth.
pairs.self_check: Did your tongue touch your teeth for दाल? If it sounded like डाल, keep the tongue forward.

a.tip: जीभ की नोक ऊपर मोड़कर तालू को छुएँ।

b.tip: जीभ की नोक ऊपर के दाँतों के पीछे छुए।

pairs.label: आ / आँ
pairs.listen_hint: Play each a few times. With ँ, some air goes through the nose.
pairs.reveal_hint: With ँ the vowel also goes through the nose. Touch your nose and feel it hum.
pairs.self_check: Did the end of पूँछ hum through your nose? If it sounded like पूछ, let the last vowel go through the nose.

a.tip: मुँह से साफ़ स्वर, नाक बंद सी।

b.tip: वही स्वर, पर हवा नाक से भी निकले।
